narrative:
Your application was denied because the model predicts you have a 51.8% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt, meaning it sees you as more likely to struggle than succeed. This decision was driven primarily by three key factors in your academic record, with your performance in your third year of school being the most influential.

Your third-year grades placed you in the 1st decile of your class, which is significantly lower than the average 6th decile seen among students who passed the bar. This was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure, as it suggests you may have struggled with advanced coursework that is critical for bar preparation. In contrast, your LSAT score of 36 and undergraduate GPA of 3.40 both worked in your favor, pushing the prediction slightly toward passing. While your LSAT is close to the average of 37.27 for successful students, your GPA is actually higher than their average of 3.24, showing strong prior academic ability.

However, the negative impact of your low third-year class rank outweighed these positive signals. The model essentially concluded that your recent academic performance in law school is a more reliable indicator of bar success than your earlier achievements. Your family income being lower-middle class, while not among the top three factors, also differs from the majority of successful students who come from upper-middle or middle-income backgrounds, though this played a smaller role.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on strengthening your third-year academic performance. Consider retaking the LSAT to raise your score above 37, which would further support your application. You might also seek academic support or bar preparation resources early in your studies to ensure your later grades better reflect your potential.
